items.title: CVE-2026-80188
items.description: The BuddyBoss Addons plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in versions up to, and including, 1.2.1. This is due to the Social Login REST endpoint trusting unverified Apple and Facebook identity-token claims and linking an attacker-controlled provider identifier to an existing WordPress user selected by the token’s email claim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know a user’s email address to associate their provider identity with that account, including administrator accounts, and subsequently authenticate as the victim. Successful exploitation requires the BuddyBoss Platform plugin to be installed and active, with the Social Login module and selected provider enabled and configured. On sites with the separate BuddyBoss App JWT component, the vulnerable REST request can return an application token immediately.

items.title: CVE-2026-130322
items.description: The EU Order Withdrawal Button for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution requires an Administrator or Shop Manager to open the Withdrawals Preview modal and click the injected note element, which the attacker can enlarge via a retained style attribute to cover the entire note area. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

items.title: CVE-2026-130010
items.description: The Chatterbug Forms – Fast, Flexible WordPress Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the cbforms_delete_uploaded_files function in all versions up to, and including, 1.1 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Exploitation requires an administrator to delete the attacker-planted form entry, and the attacker must know or be able to guess the absolute path of a file writable by the PHP process. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

items.title: CVE-2026-129840
items.description:
In the nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee repository, the GitHub Actions workflow
.github/workflows/build_documentation.yml used the pull_request_target trigger
while checking out and executing untrusted pull request code. This allowed a
pull request from a fork to run attacker-controlled code in the base repository
context with a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write, pages: write,
pull-requests: write), enabling remote code execution in CI, token
exfiltration, and unauthorized modification of repository content and GitHub
Pages. The workflow was disabled and then rewritten to remove the issue.

items.title: CVE-2026-99804
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference

io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func after calling
io_worker_cancel_cb(). For an existing worker, that call can drop the
last worker reference and wake io_worker_exit(). If the canceling task
is preempted, the worker can be unlinked and freed by kfree_rcu() before
the callback function is inspected. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free
read in this path.

Save whether the callback belongs to an unpublished continuation worker
while its reference is still held, then use the saved result for the
conditional free. This preserves the existing accounting and frees only
the worker allocated for the canceled continuation.

items.title: CVE-2026-99803
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate()

When an IORING_OP_SOCKET request is prepared in io_socket_prep(),
sock->type retains creation flags such as SOCK_CLOEXEC and SOCK_NONBLOCK
until __sys_socket_file() masks them off with SOCK_TYPE_MASK during
execution.

However, io_socket_bpf_populate() copies sock->type into
bctx->socket.type without masking off ~SOCK_TYPE_MASK. As a result, a
cBPF filter inspecting bctx->socket.type against socket types such as
SOCK_DGRAM or SOCK_STREAM can be bypassed by ORing SOCK_CLOEXEC or
SOCK_NONBLOCK into the socket type.

Mask sock->type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK when populating bctx->socket.type.

items.title: CVE-2026-99802
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind()

When io_uring_register(2) is invoked with fd == -1, it dispatches
directly to io_uring_register_blind() without checking
current->io_uring_restrict.

As a result, a task with per-task register restrictions installed via
IORING_REGISTER_RESTRICTIONS can still invoke blind registration opcodes
such as IORING_REGISTER_SEND_MSG_RING even when those opcodes are not in
the task's allowed register_op bitmap.

Check current->io_uring_restrict->register_op in
io_uring_register_blind() before dispatching blind registration opcodes.
